Linux is definitely better than Windows / MacOS, but it's not "the best operating system".

  • The "best OS" would be genuine free software: no restrictions, no lawyers, no strings attached. GNU / GPL is a communist hijacking of free software! A copyfree open source OS like BSD or HaikuOS is better in terms of ideological and legal freedom.

  • The "best OS" is one tailor-fit for your device. Right now Linux is a "jack of all trades", from small chip systems to supercomputers. Making the same codebase do absolutely adds complexity and potential bloat. By analogy: it's better to have a truck, a bus, a boat, a bicycle, a tank, and a race car, instead of one very complicated vehicle that tries to transform into all those things on demand.

  • The "best OS" should be written in a modern programming language, which would make it much easier for people to read and audit the code to make sure it's safe and reliable. C is very fast, but languages like Rust are catching up, and this performance edge is irrelevant in many situations outside the kernel (i.e. the inevitable GNU userland running on top of Linux).

Point #2 "Secure" is allright, but why does every article writing about how awesome Linux is, when it comes to this point, usually write this; "you dont need antivirus". And typically never anything else...
